# Elgato script functions

Functions for C# (`Cb.Call`) and Python (a `cb` method each, or `cb.call`). See [Script functions](index.md) for how to use them.

## elgato.cameraHub.isAvailable

Checks whether Cuebot can control webcam settings on this computer. Right now this works on Linux.

**Gives back:** true when webcam control works here, otherwise false.

=== "C#"

    ```csharp
    var answer = await Cb.Call("elgato.cameraHub.isAvailable");
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    answer = cb.elgato_camera_hub_is_available()
    ```

## elgato.cameraHub.set

Changes one picture setting on your webcam, like brightness or zoom. Fails with an error when the webcam or setting is not found.

| Value | In Python | What to put in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `device` | `device` | Optional. Which webcam: its name, id or device path. Leave it out (or empty) for the first webcam. "All" means every webcam. |
| `control` | `control` | The setting: brightness, contrast, saturation, sharpness, focus, pan, tilt, whiteBalance, zoom, autoFocus, autoWhiteBalance, autoExposure, antiFlicker, mirror or flip. |
| `value` | `value` | The new value as a number, like 60. Zoom is 100-400 percent. On/off settings take 1 (on) or 0 (off). antiFlicker also takes "Off", "50 Hz", "60 Hz" or "Auto". |
| `adjust` | `adjust` | Optional. true adds the value to the current one instead. Default false. |

**Gives back:** The new value of the setting (from the first webcam).

=== "C#"

    ```csharp
    var answer = await Cb.Call("elgato.cameraHub.set", new { control = "zoom", value = 150 });
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    answer = cb.elgato_camera_hub_set(control="zoom", value=150)
    ```

## elgato.cameraHub.webcams

Lists your webcams and their current picture settings.

**Gives back:** A list of webcams. Each has deviceId, deviceName, devicePath and the settings it supports, like brightness, contrast, focus, zoomValue, autoFocus, antiFlicker, mirrored and flipped.

=== "C#"

    ```csharp
    var answer = await Cb.Call("elgato.cameraHub.webcams");
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    answer = cb.elgato_camera_hub_webcams()
    ```

## elgato.lights.add

Adds an Elgato light by its network address. Handy when Cuebot does not find it on its own. Fails with an error when the light cannot be reached.

| Value | In Python | What to put in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | `address` | The light's IP address, like "192.168.1.50". You can add a port, like "192.168.1.50:9123". Find it in the Elgato Control Center app. |

**Gives back:** The light that was added, with the same details as elgato.lights.list.

=== "C#"

    ```csharp
    var answer = await Cb.Call("elgato.lights.add", new { address = "192.168.1.50" });
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    answer = cb.elgato_lights_add(address="192.168.1.50")
    ```

## elgato.lights.discover

Looks for Elgato lights on your network right now.

**Gives back:** A list of the lights that were found (same details as elgato.lights.list).

=== "C#"

    ```csharp
    var answer = await Cb.Call("elgato.lights.discover");
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    answer = cb.elgato_lights_discover()
    ```

## elgato.lights.identify

Makes Elgato lights blink, so you can see which one is which. Fails with an error when no light matches.

| Value | In Python | What to put in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `device` | `device` | Which light: its name, id or IP address. Split several with commas. "All" or empty means every light. |

**Gives back:** true when done.

=== "C#"

    ```csharp
    var answer = await Cb.Call("elgato.lights.identify", new { device = "Key Light" });
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    answer = cb.elgato_lights_identify(device="Key Light")
    ```

## elgato.lights.isRunning

Checks whether Cuebot is watching your Elgato lights right now.

**Gives back:** true while Cuebot checks your lights, otherwise false.

=== "C#"

    ```csharp
    var answer = await Cb.Call("elgato.lights.isRunning");
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    answer = cb.elgato_lights_is_running()
    ```

## elgato.lights.list

Lists every Elgato light Cuebot knows, like a Key Light or Light Strip.

**Gives back:** A list of lights. Each has deviceId, deviceName, productName, serialNumber, ipAddress, port and online. Lights that answered also have on, brightness, temperature (Kelvin), hue and saturation.

=== "C#"

    ```csharp
    var answer = await Cb.Call("elgato.lights.list");
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    answer = cb.elgato_lights_list()
    ```

## elgato.lights.rename

Gives an Elgato light a new name. The name is saved on the light itself, so Control Center shows it too.

| Value | In Python | What to put in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `device` | `device` | Which light: its name, id or IP address. |
| `name` | `name` | The new name, like "Desk Light". |

**Gives back:** true when done.

=== "C#"

    ```csharp
    var answer = await Cb.Call("elgato.lights.rename", new { device = "Key Light", name = "Desk Light" });
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    answer = cb.elgato_lights_rename(device="Key Light", name="Desk Light")
    ```

## elgato.lights.setBrightness

Changes how bright Elgato lights are. Fails with an error when no light matches.

| Value | In Python | What to put in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `device` | `device` | Which light: its name, id or IP address. Split several with commas. "All" or empty means every light. |
| `brightness` | `brightness` | How bright, 0-100 percent, like 75. |
| `adjust` | `adjust` | Optional. true adds the number to the current brightness instead (use a minus number to dim). Default false. |

**Gives back:** A list of the lights that changed, with their new details.

=== "C#"

    ```csharp
    var answer = await Cb.Call("elgato.lights.setBrightness", new { device = "Key Light", brightness = 75 });
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    answer = cb.elgato_lights_set_brightness(device="Key Light", brightness=75)
    ```

## elgato.lights.setColor

Changes the colour of Elgato lights that can show colours, like the Light Strip. Fails with an error when no light matches.

| Value | In Python | What to put in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `device` | `device` | Which light: its name, id or IP address. Split several with commas. "All" or empty means every light. |
| `hue` | `hue` | The colour, 0-360 around the colour wheel: 0 red, 120 green, 240 blue. |
| `saturation` | `saturation` | How strong the colour is, 0-100. 0 is white, 100 is full colour. |

**Gives back:** A list of the lights that changed, with their new details.

=== "C#"

    ```csharp
    var answer = await Cb.Call("elgato.lights.setColor", new { device = "Light Strip", hue = 270, saturation = 100 });
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    answer = cb.elgato_lights_set_color(device="Light Strip", hue=270, saturation=100)
    ```

## elgato.lights.setPower

Turns Elgato lights on or off. Fails with an error when no light matches.

| Value | In Python | What to put in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `device` | `device` | Which light: its name, id or IP address. Split several with commas. "All" or empty means every light. |
| `state` | `state` | Optional. "On", "Off" or "Toggle" (switch to the other one). Default "Toggle". |

**Gives back:** A list of the lights that changed, with their new details.

=== "C#"

    ```csharp
    var answer = await Cb.Call("elgato.lights.setPower", new { device = "Key Light", state = "On" });
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    answer = cb.elgato_lights_set_power(device="Key Light", state="On")
    ```

## elgato.lights.setTemperature

Changes the colour warmth of Elgato lights, from warm yellow to cool white. Fails with an error when no light matches.

| Value | In Python | What to put in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `device` | `device` | Which light: its name, id or IP address. Split several with commas. "All" or empty means every light. |
| `temperature` | `temperature` | The warmth in Kelvin, 2900 (warm) to 7000 (cool), like 4500. |
| `adjust` | `adjust` | Optional. true adds the Kelvin number to the current value instead. Default false. |

**Gives back:** A list of the lights that changed, with their new details.

=== "C#"

    ```csharp
    var answer = await Cb.Call("elgato.lights.setTemperature", new { device = "Key Light", temperature = 4500 });
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    answer = cb.elgato_lights_set_temperature(device="Key Light", temperature=4500)
    ```

## elgato.lights.start

Starts looking for Elgato lights on your network and watching them. It starts over if it was already running.

**Gives back:** true once it has started.

=== "C#"

    ```csharp
    var answer = await Cb.Call("elgato.lights.start");
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    answer = cb.elgato_lights_start()
    ```

## elgato.studio.isRunning

Checks whether the Elgato Studio app is open on this computer. Cuebot can only see it; Elgato Studio has no way to be controlled.

**Gives back:** true while Elgato Studio is running, otherwise false.

=== "C#"

    ```csharp
    var answer = await Cb.Call("elgato.studio.isRunning");
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    answer = cb.elgato_studio_is_running()
    ```
